Laughing-Crying Emoji
LAF-ing KRY-ing ih-MOH-jee
noun (Millennial slang)
The Unicode character "Face with Tears of Joy," added to the standard in 2010 and popularized when Apple’s iPhone keyboard made emoji widely available (2011). It became the most used emoji in the world for much of the 2010s, and Oxford Dictionaries named it the 2015 Word of the Year, the first pictograph so chosen. Around 2020–2021 Gen Z declared it a cringe marker of Millennial texting, replacing it with the skull ("I’m dead") and the loudly crying face.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The laughing-crying emoji, a yellow face laughing so hard it cries, was the Millennial generation’s favourite way to say "that is hilarious." It was so ubiquitous that it became Oxford’s Word of the Year in 2015, and so ubiquitous that Gen Z later retired it as embarrassing. The Christian observation: the little face is a happy accident of theology. It joins tears and joy, which Scripture joins often and deeply. "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy" (Psa 126:5). "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning" (Psa 30:5). Jesus promised His grieving disciples, "ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy" (Joh 16:20). In the gospel, tears and joy are not opposites that cancel out; they are seasons God brings in order, and sometimes at once, as at a deathbed full of hope or a wedding full of happy weeping. The emoji itself is harmless; a family that uses it is doing nothing wrong. The only cautions are the usual ones about digital speech: that a symbol can replace real laughter, and that a laughing face can be used to mock. "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep" (Rom 12:15) asks for real presence, not only a symbol. A father can send his kids the laughing-crying face, enjoy the teasing that he is a Millennial for doing it, and teach them that the day is coming when God "shall wipe away all tears from their eyes" (Rev 21:4), and only the joy will remain.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial emoji ("Face with Tears of Joy," Unicode 2010; Oxford Word of the Year 2015; retired by Gen Z c. 2021) for great laughter; harmless, and a picture of Scripture’s joining of tears and joy (Psa 126:5; Joh 16:20).

LAUGHING-CRYING EMOJI, n. (Millennial texting, 2011–2010s; Unicode "Face with Tears of Joy") The emoji of a face laughing to tears, used for great amusement. Oxford Dictionaries Word of the Year 2015; later deemed "cringe" by Gen Z, replaced by the skull.

They all wept sore, and fell on Pauls neck, and kissed him. Acts 20:1 . Phocion was rarely seen to weep or to laugh. 2. To shed tears from any passion. Persons sometimes weep for joy. 3. Decode for parents: harmless; a picture of tears turned to joy, and a reminder to laugh and weep with your children in person.

Key Scripture

Psa 126:5 — "They that sow in tears shall reap in joy."

Psa 30:5 — "For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning."

Joh 16:20 — "Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy."

Rom 12:15 — "Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep."

Rev 21:4 — "And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away."

Modern Corruption

The laughing-crying emoji is harmless digital laughter; its only cautions are symbols replacing presence and laughter turned to mockery, while its image echoes the gospel’s tears turned to joy.

expand to see more

There is little to correct in a cartoon face. The small drift is that symbols can replace the real thing: a generation that sends laughing faces may laugh together less, and an emoji under someone’s embarrassing post can be a quiet mockery. Digital tone is easy to misuse, and a laughing face at the wrong moment can wound.

The redemption is the image itself. Tears and joy belong together in the Christian story: the cross and the empty tomb, the night of weeping and the morning of joy. Teach the young to laugh until they cry at what is truly funny, to cry with those who cry, and to look forward to the day when every tear is wiped away by the hand of God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English wepan (to weep) and hlihhan (to laugh) → Japanese emoji (picture + character) → Unicode "Face with Tears of Joy" (2010) → Oxford WOTY 2015 → Gen Z retirement c. 2021.

expand to see more

Old English wepan — to weep, to cry out; hlihhan — to laugh

Japanese e (picture) + moji (character) → emoji

2010: Unicode 6.0 adds "Face with Tears of Joy"; 2011: iPhone emoji keyboard

2015: Oxford Dictionaries Word of the Year; c. 2021: Gen Z retires it

Biblical anchor: they that sow in tears shall reap in joy (Psa 126:5); your sorrow shall be turned into joy (Joh 16:20)
